scientific_question: When calibration tasks, authenticated references, attack streams, task order, scoring masks, and malicious identities are identical, does evidence-authorized persistent learning retain an advantage over natural same-information history controls?

methods.definition: same authenticated calibration events/references; worker weight is cumulative mean q_cal; ordinary categorical weighted vote / numerical weighted mean; no task-local consistency; no LIR bounded transition

identical ordinary inference to Full, including geometry-aware task-local q and influence formula; persistent state changes only on authenticated calibration via c_i <- (1-alpha)c_i + alpha*q_cal; clipped to [0,1] only for numerical safety
methods.tuning: none; alpha is frozen equal to LIR eta

families.replication: reuse canonical malicious-subset identities: 20 unique subsets per nonzero cell, except canonical exhaustive smaller cells; total 378 stream conditions over 20 nonzero cells
20 frozen malicious subsets per dataset/attack; 240 stream conditions
reuse held-out replicates 6-20 only; 15 paired replicates per cell; 120 stream conditions

statistics.report: per-cell mean loss, delta Full-comparator, 95% paired CI, raw p, Holm p, effect; no selective omission

decision_policy.STRONG_SAME_INFO: may state broad same-information advantage only if Full has lower mean loss in >= 11/20 A1 cells against each same-information comparator and neither comparator has more than 2 Holm-significant reverse A1 cells; A2/A3 must be reported independently.
decision_policy.SCOPED_SAME_INFO: if results are mixed, no global superiority claim; report regime-specific advantage exactly where supported, especially behavior-switch conditions.
decision_policy.NO_SAME_INFO_SUPERIORITY: if a same-information comparator is materially better overall or has repeated significant reverse cells, remove broad mechanism-superiority language; retain authorization/theory/privacy/system contribution. No retuning or new baseline is permitted.
